label: Alienware
description: Matte black gaming chrome, angular clip-path-cut corners, and a single AlienFX cyan light strip down the rail.

label: Aperture Science
description: Sterile Aperture Science test-chamber off-white and grey, with portal blue/orange as the only saturated colours — Portal's signature palette split.

label: Aqua
description: macOS X 10.6 Snow Leopard: candy-gloss buttons, a 3px pinstripe texture on every panel, brushed-metal chrome.

label: Barbie
description: Hot-pink glamour with 999px-radius glossy pill chrome, gold sparkle headings, and mint-green success states with dark text.

label: Bloomberg Terminal
description: Black-and-amber monospace terminal density — every UI element, not just numbers, set in Consolas, at --density: 0.7.

label: Blue Future
description: Deep-space navy HUD with cyan neon glow — the catalog's baseline sci-fi console look.

label: Cue Lab
description: A flat, glow-free live-show console: hairline grids and a single amber accent, the deliberate opposite of blue-future's neon.

label: Cyber-Goth
description: Pitch-black club vinyl gloss with toxic neon green and hot purple sharing the accent role.

label: Death Star Terminal
description: True #000000 black with glowing solid indicator blocks and zero borders or shadows — a terminal aesthetic distilled to almost nothing.

label: Hot Wheels
description: Blister-pack orange on track-black with a diagonal flame-stripe app bar and a checkered-flag status strip.

label: iMac G3
description: Translucent ribbed Bondi Blue plastic with three swappable fruit-colour variants (Blueberry/Grape/Tangerine) via data-variant.

label: International Rescue
description: Gerry Anderson's Thunderbirds (1965): a cream 1960s atomic-age control console with navy IR bands, gold trim and flat Technicolor craft-colour lamps.

label: LCARS
description: Star Trek's Okuda-designed on-screen computer: candy-coloured pill blocks on true black with a signature elbow-curve rail.

label: LEGO Classic
description: Primary-colour blocks, thick borders, and circular corner studs on every panel — a physical brick, not just a palette.

label: Material
description: Google Material Design: flat bold colour and a layered elevation shadow system in place of gloss or blur, underlined text fields.

label: The Matrix
description: Phosphor-green #00FF41 digital-rain cascade on black — matching the reference on-screen code's actual hex.

label: MS-DOS
description: Blue-and-white text-mode Norton Commander: double-line box borders, bright cyan/yellow as the only two 'bright' VGA colours.

label: NERV Terminal
description: NERV's bunker terminal: deep black, hazard-stripe orange, and a dark crimson danger state reserved for real alerts.

label: Nokia 3310
description: The reflective yellow-green monochrome LCD of the 3310/3210 era — no backlight colour, no anti-aliasing, selection reads as a hard colour invert.

label: Pip-Boy 3000
description: Fallout's Pip-Boy 3000: monochrome phosphor green with a scanline overlay — every state reads as one green, on purpose.

label: Steampunk
description: Polished brass and stitched leather, riveted copper panels, and functioning-instrument ornamentation — sight-glass meters, needled gauge readouts.

label: Teletext
description: BBC Ceefax-era teletext: the fixed 8-colour broadcast palette on solid black, zero gradients, zero anti-aliasing, flat colour-block headers.

label: TRON
description: The Grid's electric cyan line-grid on black, with clip-path-cut angular corners standing in for the film's beveled edges.

label: Vaporwave
description: Outrun synthwave: a magenta-to-cyan gradient clipped to heading text, over a deep-purple void with a perspective grid-floor horizon.

label: Weyland-Yutani
description: Alien-franchise corporate/industrial: warm near-black hardware, bone-beige label plates, amber phosphor readouts, and hazard yellow/black striping reserved for danger states.

label: Windows 7 Aero
description: Real backdrop-filter glass blur over the Aero desktop gradient — translucent, not just a lighter opaque fill like Luna's gloss.

label: WinAmp Classic
description: The steel-gray Winamp 2.x skin: tiny uppercase labels and llama-green LCD-style readouts.

label: Windows 95
description: Classic beveled 3D gray dialog chrome on the #008080-ish teal desktop, bevels inverting light-to-dark on press.

label: Windows XP (Luna)
description: The default Luna Blue XP desktop: glossy round-cornered blue chrome, with the Start-button green reserved for primary actions.

label: Windows Media Player 11
description: WMP11's black-glass skin with a cool blue glow — the last Windows Media Player skin before the Zune-era flattening.

label: XBMC
description: The original Xbox Media Center — a near-black home-theatre shell, a horizontal top menu, and a glowing blue underline marking the selected item.

label: XMB (Cross Media Bar)
description: The PlayStation 3 / PSP dashboard — a deep-blue wave gradient, thin glowing selection bars, and translucent panels floating over it.
